walkthrough:
Equate the two functions to find points of intersection $A$ and $B$:
$$3 - 2x = 4 - 3\sqrt{x} \implies 2x - 3\sqrt{x} + 1 = 0$$

Substitute $u = \sqrt{x}$ to form a quadratic in $u$:
$$2u^2 - 3u + 1 = 0 \implies (2u - 1)(u - 1) = 0$$
$$u = \frac{1}{2} \quad \text{or} \quad u = 1$$

Square both roots to find the $x$-coordinates:
$$\sqrt{x} = \frac{1}{2} \implies x = \frac{1}{4} = 0.25$$
$$\sqrt{x} = 1 \implies x = 1$$
$$(\text{Intersection } x\text{-coordinates: } x = \frac{1}{4}, \quad 1)$$

hints: Evaluate at $1$ and $\frac{1}{4}$ to find area $\frac{1}{16} = 0.0625$.
walkthrough:
Set up the definite integral for the region enclosed between the line $y = 3 - 2x$ and the curve $y = 4 - 3\sqrt{x}$ from $x = \frac{1}{4}$ to $x = 1$:
$$\text{Area} = \int_{1/4}^1 \left[(3 - 2x) - (4 - 3x^{\frac{1}{2}})\right] dx = \int_{1/4}^1 \left(-1 - 2x + 3x^{\frac{1}{2}}\right) dx$$

Evaluate at the lower limit $x = \frac{1}{4}$ and subtract:
$$F(1/4) = -\frac{1}{4} - \left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^2 + 2\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}} = -\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{16} + 2\left(\frac{1}{8}\right) = -\frac{5}{16} + \frac{1}{4} = -\frac{1}{16}$$
$$\text{Area} = 0 - \left(-\frac{1}{16}\right) = \frac{1}{16} \quad (= 0.0625\text{ square units})$$
